name: Suba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Ochieng, Lilian Akoth; Khasandi, Vicky; Mutiti, James. 2013. A description of the morphosyntactic structure of the Suba language. Open Science Repository Language and Linguistics, e23050474. doi:10.7392/openaccess.23050474
sources.note: Nothing; noun classes, agreement, verb morphology, word order (Mfangano data).
Uncited paragraph claims two tones (high marked with acute, low with grave/unmarked), nothing on stress; tagged 'citation needed' -- not a usable source.

sources.citation: Ochieng Aluoch Connie; Lwangale, David Wafula; Katie, Hylean Okoth; Indangasi, Roselyn Dembeko. 2023. A study of phonological processes in Dholuo and Suba languages. International Journal of Social Science & Humanities Research 6(6): 92-104. doi:10.5281/zenodo.8119807
sources.note: Nothing usable. The one tone sentence ('a tonal language with four tones') refers to Dholuo; the Suba paragraph ('11 consonants and 7 vowels', V/CV syllables) is lifted from the uncited Wikipedia article. No stress statement for Suba.

sources.citation: Sande, Walter Ochieng. 2023. Constraints interaction in the syllabification in Olusuba. Journal of Linguistics, Literary and Communication Studies 2(1): 28-40. doi:10.58721/jltcs.v2i1.266
sources.note: Nothing; nine syllable types, moraicity, NC onsets. No mention of stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Ongaro, Merceline A. 2019. A semantic analysis of Suba kinship terminologies. MA thesis, University of Nairobi.
sources.note: Nothing; useful only for the dialect list (Olwivwang'ano of Mfangano etc.) and for the reference to Matta 2011 (BTL primer on Olusuba letters and sounds).

sources.citation: Sande, W.O.; Ondondo, E.A.; Rew, F.O. 2019. An Optimality analysis of hiatus resolution strategies in Olusuba. International Journal of Linguistics and Communication 7(1): 29-39. doi:10.15640/ijlc.v7n1a4
sources.note: Nothing; glide formation and vowel assimilation in OT. No prosody.

sources.citation: Sande, Walter Ochieng; Ondondo, Emily Ayieta; Rew, Francis Owino. 2019. A study of vowel length in Olusuba. International Journal of English Language and Linguistics Research 7(3): 45-56.
sources.note: Nothing. Describes five vowels, underlying vs derived vowel length (glide formation + compensatory lengthening); the only mentions of tone concern Mande/Yoruba in the literature review. No statement on Olusuba stress, accent or tone.
